drills.coachNote: Before you recapture on f8, notice White is one move from playing Rxa1 and just winning your loose bishop back for free, since nothing on the board defends a1. The fix was Bd4+, giving check first: the bishop escapes to safety while forcing Kh1, and only then do you play Kxf8 with the a1 problem already solved, continuing on to win more material with Nxf4. drills.coachNote: White's idea is simple: shove the e-pawn to e5, gaining a free tempo on your knight since the queen on f3 is already supporting that push. Playing Nf6 walks straight into that plan — the knight has to hop away again right when White attacks it, and if you ever answer with something else like developing the other knight instead of moving it, the pawn just captures on f6 outright and wins the piece. Nc6 avoids all of this by developing toward the center without handing White a free attacking move, letting the game continue calmly with Nh3, h6, c3, e5, Bc4. In the opening, don't put a piece where your opponent can hit it with tempo for nothing.
